note: THE FIRST NON-MALE CARD IN THE PROJECT, and the first to carry `base_tags`. MEASURED, not predicted: her sheet, her 16-view turnaround and her LoRA sweep all render an unambiguously teenage girl. Without base_tags, compose.py:1482 appends the module constant MALE = 'male focus, mature male, masculine' to slot 2 of her prompt. base_tags replaces it with 'female focus, teenage girl, slender' and that is confirmed in the resolved prompt. | BASE_TAGS IS ONLY HALF THE FIX AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT ON THIS CARD. workflows/22_anime_kf_ipadapter.json node 6 hard-codes the negative '1girl, girl, female, feminine, breasts, ...' and scripts/short.py plumbs NO negative input on either keyframe workflow (compose.py:71-73 and 1836-1841 both say so). Every anime render the film pipeline produces therefore carries 'female' in its negative and no card or film can override it. Her sheet, turnaround and sweeps were all rendered with that negative replaced by hand. SHE WILL NOT RENDER CORRECTLY THROUGH compile.py -> short.py until a negative input is wired. That is a renderer defect, deliberately not worked around on this card. | CORRECTED 2026-08-04, THE RENDERER DEFECT IS FIXED AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS NOW HISTORY. scripts/short.py grew _negative(), which drops from the shipped negative any clause whose every word also appears in the positive prompt. Verified by ASSEMBLING THE REAL GRAPH, not by reading code: a beat of hers now sends a negative with '1girl, girl, female' removed, while VIRO's and MANAGER's come back byte-identical to the shipped workflow. NOT YET VERIFIED IN PIXELS - no film of hers has been rendered end to end, because the box was queue-bound. The first person to render her should look and say whether it worked. | ALSO FIXED 2026-08-04: `lora_strength_measured` now REACHES the renderer. It never did. studio/compile.py emits character_lora_weights and short.py reads it, so a beat of hers loads her weights at 0.5 rather than the 0.85 that was measured to destroy her setting. Confirmed on the assembled graph: node 90 strength_model 0.5. | SIDECUT NEVER RENDERED. 'sidecut' is in `tags` and is absent from the sheet, from all 16 turnaround views, and from all six sweep cells at every strength. Long hair plus a single braid wins the argument every time. The tag is left in place as an honest record of a request the engine refuses; do not count it as an identity marker. | THE NECKTIE IS BLACK IN THE TRAINING SET, NOT RED. wear_tags asks for a red necktie; the sheet and all 16 views rendered it black, so the LoRA learned black. At strength 0.5-0.85 the tie is pulled back toward red by the tags, which is why the sweep cells disagree with the turnaround. The star pin also rendered far larger and more ornate than 'a small red enamel pin', and gold rather than red. | THE GARMENT LIVES IN wear_tags, NOT IN tags. | `prose` is the VISUAL description used by the qwen engine; `desc` is narrative and tells an image model nothing it can draw.
lora_verdict: MEASURED by looking at studio/samples/cast/nika_sweep.jpg - two scenes, three strengths, one seed per row, only strength varying. WHAT THE LoRA ADDS OVER TAGS ALONE: the tags alone already carry heterochromia, silver hair, the braid and a blazer, so the control is not a stranger. What the LoRA adds is the SPECIFIC garment and face from the sheet - at 0.0 she wears a NAVY blazer, at 0.5 and 0.85 she wears the training set's grey blazer with red piping, the ornate gold star, and the facial scar appears. It is neither undertrained nor overfit: every cell is a new scene, not a returned training portrait. WHAT IT COSTS: the background, and the cost is severe at 0.85. The 'sunlit field' row is the blunt version - at 0.0 a lush golden-green field with depth and bokeh, at 0.5 a flatter but intact green field, at 0.85 a DARK GREY VOID with a strip of grass, which is her turnaround set's flat blue-grey studio backdrop imported wholesale. The neon street degrades the same way, from a deep reflective alley to flat grey outlines. USE 0.5. 0.85 is the short.py default (character_lora_weight) and for this character it destroys the setting; 0.5 keeps the face and gives the scene back.
prose: a seventeen-year-old girl with waist-length silver-blonde hair in a single braid over her right shoulder, the left side of her head shaved close, one green eye and one amber eye, a thin scar splitting her right eyebrow
negative_fix_verdict: RENDERED AND LOOKED AT, 2026-08-04, and it corrects the claim it was meant to confirm. The cast wave reported the shipped negative in workflows/22 - which opens '1girl, girl, female, feminine, breasts' - as a BLOCKER that made a female character unrenderable. Rendered at one seed with and without short.py's _negative() fix, NIKA comes back an unmistakably female character BOTH WAYS: white hair, heterochromia, blazer, side braid. The contradiction is real and removing it is right, but it did not prevent the render. 'Blocker' was overstated; 'contradiction worth removing' is accurate. The male control had nothing dropped from its negative in either cell, so the rule left the existing characters' prompts untouched, which is the property that mattered. Evidence: studio/samples/cast/negative_fix_proof.jpg
nonanime_verdict: RENDERED AND LOOKED AT, 2026-08-04, studio/_tools/cast_style.py. THE PHOTOGRAPHIC ROUTE WORKS AND ITS COST IS HER EYES. Her anime sheet was handed to Qwen-Image-Edit in four places with 'waist-up photograph' in the prompt and returned flat cel illustration 4 of 4; the photographic sheet, same prompt string, same seeds, same graph apart from which PNG node 8 loads, returned a photograph 4 of 4 with the laundromat, snowfield, library and market street all fully intact. It is one recognisable young woman across all four, and the SCAR splitting her right eyebrow carries 4 of 4. THE HETEROCHROMIA DOES NOT. Counted twice at full crop resolution off samples/cast_style/nika_eyes.jpg, one green and one amber eye is legible in the library and market cells and absent in the laundromat and snowfield cells - 2 of 4, against 5 of 5 for the character LoRA on the anime path. A photograph draws an eye at the size an eye actually is, so a marker that only reads because illustration exaggerates it does not survive the trip. ALSO NOTE THE SIDE FLIPPED: her photographic sheet puts amber on the VIEWER'S RIGHT, the mirror of the anime training set, and every downstream photographic cell inherits the sheet's side. Nothing in the card names a side, so this is not a defect, but the two routes will disagree with each other and a film cannot mix them. PAINTERLY ON THE ANIME ENGINE: THE SETTING IS IPAdapter 0.0 WITH HER LoRA AT 0.5, AND AT THAT SETTING EXACTLY ONE OF THE FOUR STYLES ACTUALLY LANDS. CORRECTED 2026-08-04 ON REVIEW - a first draft of this line said watercolour, ink_wash and oil_painting all land, and the run's own numbers refute it. Only INK_WASH changes the medium: its sat_mean collapses to 7.9 in the library (control 36.7) and 19.6 at market_street (control 64.8), and looked at it is a genuine monochrome ink wash in both places. Watercolour, oil_painting and oil_painterly sit AT OR ABOVE their own control's saturation in BOTH places - library 58.9 / 59.4 / 67.0 against 36.7, market 58.4 / 73.3 / 61.5 against 64.8 - and looked at they are animagine cel with different LIGHTING, not paintings. Do not promise a user watercolour or oil on this path yet. THE SHEET IS STILL THE KILL SWITCH, and for the one style that lands it kills almost immediately: ink_wash saturation runs 8 / 27 / 28 / 26 at IPAdapter 0.0 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 in the library against a no-style control of 34-43, and its hue distance from the unstyled cell falls 51.4 -> 16.5 over the first step there. (The often-quoted 117.6 -> 18.6 is MARKET_STREET's hue run, not the library's; the saturation figures beside it are the library's. Two places, one sentence, in the first draft.) At 0.6 all five style columns are the same washed-out picture and the room has gone with them. Identity holds at 0.0 on the LoRA alone. Evidence: samples/cast_style/nika_paint_market_street.jpg, nika_paint_library_reading_room.jpg. STYLE LoRA ON QWEN, AND THIS ONE REFUTES A RECORDED CLAIM: with illustration-1.0-qwen-image at 1.5 and NO reference at all she comes back painted AND on model, heterochromia and scar both present, 2 of 2. With her photographic sheet as the reference at the same strength she comes back painted and A DIFFERENT WOMAN, dark eyes and no scar, 2 of 2. The project's note that this LoRA needs a reference to hold identity was measured on VIRO and does not generalise to her. Evidence: samples/cast_style/nika_styleLoRA_faces.jpg.
sheet_photo_verdict: The sheet renders her card faithfully: silver-blonde braid, grey blazer, red necktie (RED, not the black the LoRA learned), red enamel star pin at roughly the size the card asks for rather than the ornate gold one the anime sheet drew, one green and one amber eye, and the scar splitting her right eyebrow. The sidecut is absent, as it is everywhere else in this project.
